clue.text: Neat deterrent on the way

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is a barrier set in a road that stops livestock from straying across it

explanation.surface: Something tidy that discourages people along a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like 'tidy', but it is the old word for cattle (as in neatsfoot oil); the deterrent is the barred pit across a road that livestock will not cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A road grid of bars over a pit keeps farm animals from crossing, deterring cows on the road.

clue.text: Guy with chilblain?

definitions.meaning: a guy is a man or fellow
chilblains crack and roughen the skin, and a crack in cold-damaged skin is also called by this word

explanation.surface: A man suffering from a winter sore.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a fellow, and roughened, cracked skin from the cold.

clue.text: Mark of approval for credit

definitions.meaning: the check mark a teacher puts beside a right answer
buying on account, informally 'on the slate'

explanation.surface: A sign of approval given in exchange for credit.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English the check mark is called a tick, and 'on tick' means on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A check mark is the sign of approval, and informal British usage calls deferred payment by the same word.

clue.text: Language of besotted boy

parts.note: lad means boy
besotted means in love, and love is O (zero in tennis), giving IN and O

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken by an infatuated young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Besotted boy' is a boy in love: LAD + IN + O, with love as O from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladino is the Judeo-Spanish tongue of Sephardic Jews.

clue.text: Mitchell's airborne romance

parts.note: Margaret Mitchell's novel of the American Civil War, its title read literally as carried off on a breeze

explanation.surface: A love story by a writer named Mitchell set in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Mitchell wrote the famous Civil War romance; 'airborne' is a playful reading of its title as something blown away.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Margaret Mitchell's famous novel, a sweeping love story, also means blown away by a breeze.

clue.text: Book first-class? One has to change!

indicators.note: the letters are required to change their order, which marks them as anagram fodder

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A top-quality book, but someone needs to alter it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' shuffles AI (A1), I (one) and HAS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetic book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Chief god of ocean noise

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for ocean
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: The principal deity of the roaring sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the ruler of the gods in Norse mythology.

clue.text: Certified firm

definitions.meaning: certified in the sense of officially established or ascertained
firm in the sense of resolute

explanation.surface: A company with official approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a business, but here it is an adjective meaning resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: officially established, and resolute in purpose.

clue.text: In his business, runners may scatter

definitions.text: In his business, runners may scatter

indicators.note: to scatter is to spread the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A trade in which sprinters might disperse.
explanation.walkthrough: Runners here are plant shoots that spread along the ground, a gardener's stock in trade; 'scatter' rearranges RUNNERS MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant grower raises young stock, and runners are shoots that spread across his beds.

clue.text: One may indicate sharp pieces of calcite and compound

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture, so the words calcite and 'and' are combined and remixed

explanation.surface: Something that shows sharp fragments of a mineral and a chemical mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces of' reinforces the breaking up of CALCITE; 'compound' mixes it with AND. In music the sign for a sharp, flat or natural not in the key signature has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical notation, a sign outside the key signature can mark a note as sharp.

clue.text: Prison activity

explanation.surface: Things to do in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: slang for jail, and a bustle or commotion.

clue.text: Mallard, for example, can be seen still in York

definitions.text: Mallard, for example, can be seen still in York

parts.words: Mallard, for example, can be seen still in York
parts.note: Mallard is the record-breaking locomotive kept at the National Railway Museum in York, not a duck

explanation.surface: Ducks may be spotted in York.
explanation.walkthrough: Mallard is not a duck but the record-holding 1938 locomotive, displayed at the National Railway Museum in York.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallard is a famous coal-fired locomotive preserved in a York museum.

clue.text: Rocket scientist climbs aboard-to go around Sussex, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for climbs is made to go around another piece, enclosing it

parts.note: steps means climbs
Sussex is a breed of chicken, so an example is a hen
aboard means on

explanation.surface: A space researcher goes on board and then tours a southern county.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket is the 1829 locomotive, not a spacecraft; Sussex is a county but also a chicken breed.
explanation.definitionFit: George and Robert Stephenson built the pioneering locomotive called Rocket.

clue.text: Woman's appointment about noon with abominable sort

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the letter for noon, enclosing it
an appointment is an arrangement, so the letters of woman's are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters of the word as written, including its S

explanation.surface: A lady has a midday date with a dreadful person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appointment' rearranges WOMANS to SOWMAN, which goes 'about' N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abominable Snowman, or yeti, is the legendary beast of the Himalayas.

clue.text: Performer who needs no backing

parts.note: backing means accompaniment from other musicians, not financial support

explanation.surface: An entertainer who does not need financial sponsors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' suggests money, but in music it is accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer or player performing alone has no accompanying musicians.

clue.text: Perfectly good beginners?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, having no faults or sins

explanation.surface: Beginners who are flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO VICES, the word means without faults.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: free of faults when split in two, and newcomers to a field.

clue.text: Hide pictures of military display

definitions.meaning: hide means skin, so these are images inked into the skin
an evening show of drumming and marching by troops

explanation.surface: Concealing images of an army show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' is not a verb but skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: inked images on skin, and an evening show of drums and marching troops.

clue.text: Newmarket individual said to be husky

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken rather than read, so what follows is a sound-alike

parts.note: Newmarket is the English home of horse racing, so one of its residents is a racehorse

explanation.surface: A man from a racing town is reported to sound rough-voiced.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is a Suffolk town famous as the centre of British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, gravelly voice is described as husky.

clue.text: Come near to proficiency and friendliness

parts.note: approach means come near to
ability means proficiency or skill

explanation.surface: Getting close to skill and warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Being easy to talk to is a kind of friendliness.

clue.text: Hard times, perhaps, for such belief in divinities

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Difficult periods may drive people toward faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges H (hard) with TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is faith in a god or gods.

clue.text: What ails boy in springtime?

indicators.note: in places the boy inside the month

parts.note: May is a spring month
lad means boy

explanation.surface: What troubles a young man in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness is what ails a person.

clue.text: A scene set for a Roman dramatist

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A stage scene is arranged for a playwright of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges SCENE into SENEC; the A then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger wrote Latin tragedies.

clue.text: Crackling on telly still?

definitions.meaning: interference heard or seen on a television or radio

explanation.surface: Is the television still making crackling noises?
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like 'yet' but means motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: electrical interference on a broadcast, and motionless.

clue.text: Stories about New Testament money then?

indicators.note: the stories go about the letters for the New Testament, enclosing them

parts.note: tales means stories

explanation.surface: Tales of biblical cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' signals an old sense: in biblical times a talent was a weight of silver used as money, as in the parable.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ancient world a talent was a large unit of silver used as currency.

clue.text: Section of collapsed dome in church recess

indicators.note: only a section of the words is taken, so the answer is lifted out of them

explanation.surface: Part of a fallen dome ends up in a church alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular vaulted end of a church is a recess at its east end.

clue.text: Role learned in standard time

parts.note: par means the standard level

explanation.surface: An actor learns a role in the usual time.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's role is the character played.

clue.text: Old foreign coins buried in Treasure Island

indicators.note: the coins are buried within the words, so the answer is concealed inside them

explanation.surface: Ancient money is buried on Stevenson's island.
explanation.definitionFit: Reis were former Portuguese and Brazilian money units.

clue.text: His worship of Magritte, as restored?

indicators.note: restored suggests a painting being reworked, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A painting by the Belgian surrealist being restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges MAGRITTE AS. 'His worship' is the formal title for a British magistrate, not religious worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Your Worship is the form of address for a justice of the peace in Britain.

clue.text: Article, fashionable brought back in one of Columbus's ships

indicators.note: brought back means the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A fashionable article is returned aboard an explorer's ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of' signals the definition is a single example: the Niña was the smallest of the three ships on the 1492 voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niña sailed with the Pinta and Santa Maria in 1492.

clue.text: Day-insects forming into organized groups

indicators.note: the letters are forming into a new arrangement, which marks an anagram

explanation.surface: Mayflies gathering into organised swarms.
explanation.definitionFit: Syndicates are associations of people or firms joined for a common purpose.
